mount.description: The name this display is reached under on the colony's one listener: the page is /<mount>/, the socket /<mount>/live/websocket. Required, and owned -- a second display takes its own via override_params, or the second registers nothing and says so. A change takes effect on the cell's next life.

identity_header.description: Request header a reverse proxy in front puts the viewer's identity in, e.g. X-Forwarded-User. When set, its value on a socket's upgrade request rides as hop.user_id on every semantic event of that connection. Empty by default: a header a client can set without a proxy is not an identity.

external_timeout_ms.description: Operation timeout for I/O this cell initiates, in milliseconds.

description.purpose: The display cell: it is reached at /<mount>/ on the colony's one listener, holds the object tree and the component library in its own cell.db, renders server-side into a materialised LiveView tree and pushes exactly one diff per applied write to whoever is looking at the affected page.
description.use_when: One instance per display. The mount is required and owned -- give a second instance its own via override_params. There is no port and no bind: the colony's listener hands this cell the connections whose first path segment names its mount, and this cell type never authenticates and never will (R-W8-2), so whatever stands in front of that listener is the whole access story.
description.not_in_scope: No auth, no TLS, no listener of its own, no routing beyond its mount (the pages table is the only route source; there is no cell.surface key any more -- it was removed with the /surface/* path it declared, and a tree still carrying one is refused at boot by name), no application logic. It renders what it was sent and reports what a person did.
description.emits_meaning: Three emission shapes, hence no required hop key: (a) a tool_result reply per op -- hop carries operation, rows_affected, duration_ms and error_code when the op was refused; (b) a bundle reply for two or more tool_call turns -- hop.operation is 'bundle', rows_affected is the sum, and bundle_errors is stamped unconditionally, 0 included, while the body carries a results[] slot with one metadata entry per leg in call order; (c) a semantic browser event as a SOURCE emission on hop.route 'event' -- header event_name, session_id (the page load's own id), page_route and, when identity_header names a header the proxy sent, user_id, body carrying the event slot beside the turn. Promoting session_id into context.session_id is the entry edge's set_context job, exactly as with the proxy cell.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns carrying the ops. One turn is a single operation, two or more are a bundle -- tool_call TURNS are counted, so prose beside a call does not change how the call is answered.
examples: object.create {parent: 'root', component: 'text', props: {body: 'hello'}} -> one tool_result, one diff to every viewer of the page that contains 'root'

a button press in the browser -> a source emission with hop {route: 'event', event_name: 'action', session_id, page_route: '/'}, carrying user_id as well when identity_header is set and the proxy sent it
